Ten places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes
into a real Lakeshore filing. All ten were checked and loading at the time this page was
written.

- **[21 CFR 606.171, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-606/subpart-F/section-606.171)**
  — the full section this lesson quotes from: who must report (a), how (d), where (e), and
  how this duty relates to other FDA regulations (f). eCFR's "current as of" banner is useful
  for confirming you're reading the in-force version.

- **[21 CFR 606.171, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the same section, formatted for quick paragraph-by-paragraph reading, useful as a second
  copy to cross-check a quote against.

- **[FDA, General Instructions for Completing the Biological Product Deviation Report (BPDR) — Form FDA 3486](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/general-instructions-completing-biological-product-deviation-report-bpdr-form-fda-3486)**
  — FDA's own public instructions page for the form this lesson's walkthrough describes at a
  conceptual level. Useful if you ever need the actual field-by-field layout, which this
  lesson deliberately doesn't reproduce.

- **[FDA, Instructions for Using the eBPDR System](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/instructions-using-ebpdr-system)**
  — FDA's own instructions for the electronic filing channel 606.171(e)(2) describes as
  "CBER's electronic Web-based application." Worth reading before recommending electronic
  filing to a team that's never used it.

- **[FDA, Biological Product Deviations](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/biological-product-deviations)**
  — CBER's own landing page for the BPDR program: the starting point linking the form, the
  electronic system, the code lists, and CBER's contact points. Read it first when you need to
  confirm what CBER currently publishes. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Electronic Submission of Biological Product Deviation Reports (eBPDR)](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/electronic-submission-biological-product-deviation-reports-ebpdr)**
  — FDA's page on the electronic channel itself, the one 606.171(e)(2) calls CBER's web-based
  application. Pair it with the eBPDR instructions above before recommending electronic filing
  to a team that has never used it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Biological Product Deviation Reporting and HCT/P Deviation Reporting: Deviation Codes](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/biological-product-deviation-reporting-and-hctp-deviation-reporting-deviation-codes)**
  — FDA's published list of the deviation codes used when completing a report. Useful when your
  QA classifies a deviation like BPD-0512 and you want to see the code vocabulary CBER itself
  uses; the lesson deliberately does not reproduce it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[AABB, Ask the FDA and CMS/CLIA, 2020 Virtual Annual Meeting (transcript, PDF)](https://www.aabb.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/regulatory/2020-ask-the-fda-and-clia-transcript.pdf)**
  — a transcript of an FDA question-and-answer session at AABB's annual meeting that includes
  CBER discussion of BPDR reporting, in the blood-establishment setting. A transcript, not a
  video, and dated 2020, so confirm any specifics against the current FDA pages above. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[An Update on Field Alert Reports (FAR) and Biological Product Deviation Reports (BPDR)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EtLmHnBuNJQ)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson, also used in `escalation-criteria`; the only FDA video on BPDRs that could be found and
  verified. Part of it covers drug-side Field Alert Reports, outside this course. Verified
  embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA guidance: Biological Product Deviation Reporting for Blood and Plasma Establishments](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/biological-product-deviation-reporting-blood-and-plasma-establishments)**
  — CBER's guidance written specifically for blood and plasma establishments filing under
  606.171. It is guidance ("should"), not regulation; read it for FDA's recommendations on what
  is and isn't reportable before Lakeshore's next borderline call. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about deviation investigation, root cause and incident handling.

- **[A fresh look at an old topic: Investigations in the GMDP environment](https://mhrainspectorate.blog.gov.uk/2020/09/14/a-fresh-look-at-an-old-topic-investigations-in-the-gmdp-environment/)** (MHRA Inspectorate blog, UK regulator) — an inspectorate's candid take on what makes a deviation investigation good or weak. UK context, but the investigation habits apply to any regulator. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Deviation Management Process In GMP](https://gmpinsiders.com/deviation-management-process/)** (GMP Insiders, practitioner site) — a walk through logging, classifying, investigating and closing a deviation; useful for sanity-checking Lakeshore's own workflow. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Effective CAPA & Root Cause Investigations](https://www.rephine.com/resources/blog/understanding-investigations-root-causes-implementing-effective-capa-system)** (Rephine, consultancy; vendor content) — practical advice on getting from a symptom to a root cause and checking that the fix worked. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations Guide](https://destcert.com/resources/cissp-domain-7-security-operations/)** (Destination Certification, CISSP training company; commercial) — covers incident management (detect, respond, recover, lessons learned), the IT-security cousin of deviation handling. Supports CISSP Domain 7 (Security Operations). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
